name: Aeroparque Jorge Newbery
before:
Buenos Aires has two airports and this is the close one: 2 km north west of downtown, on the Rio de la Plata in Palermo. Domestic routes and regional South American services run from here, while most long haul international traffic uses Ezeiza well outside the city.

That split is the thing to get right. A client connecting from a long haul arrival onto an internal Argentine flight has to cross Buenos Aires between the two airports, and the traffic is not kind.

The site is compact at 138 hectares and is operated by Aeropuertos Argentina 2000.

It has been flying since 1947, on ground reclaimed from the river in 1916 after a proposal for an island airport reached by causeway was dropped. It opened as Aeroparque 17 de Octubre with a single 1,000 metre runway, and everyone still shortens the name to Aeroparque.
after:
Buenos Aires has two main airports and this is the close one, inside the city and north west of the centre. The city's tourism board puts it about 25 minutes from the main hotels. Domestic routes and regional international flights run from here, while most long-haul international traffic uses Ezeiza, well outside the city.

That split is the thing to get right. A client connecting from a long-haul arrival at Ezeiza onto a domestic flight from here has to cross Buenos Aires between the two airports. Ezeiza has some domestic flights too, so check which airport the onward flight uses.

The site is compact at 138 hectares and is run by Aeropuertos Argentina. Its name is usually shortened to Aeroparque.

claims.note: Was 'regional South American services'. The operator says regional flights to 'various countries of the Americas', so 'South American' is dropped. Current: Aviacionline (23 December 2025) lists the airlines (Aerolíneas Argentinas, American Jet, JetSMART, Flybondi, LATAM, GOL, LADE, Humming Airways, Sky, Avianca and Paranair) and 16 international destinations, and 5.2 million international passengers in 2025 (28 January 2026). FlightGlobal reported in June 2023 that Aerolíneas Argentinas would start flights to the USA from here; nothing read shows them running now, which is why the next phrase keeps 'most'.

claims.why: Softened to 'two main airports' (above) as a precaution: only the tourism board's visitor advice names exactly two airports.

claims.claim: 2 km from downtown
claims.why: Fails the coordinates check: the airport is 6.9 km in a straight line from the city centre (ratio 0.29), so no road distance can be 2 km. Wikipedia and the operator's own page both say 2 km, so the figure is not made up, but it cannot be measured from the centre and would mislead. Replaced by the tourism board's 25 minutes from the main hotels (attributed) and the direction, which holds. Flag for Andy: the operator's page repeats the figure.

claims.claim: flying since 1947, on land reclaimed in 1916, after the island-airport proposal was dropped
claims.wasBefore: It has been flying since 1947, on ground reclaimed from the river in 1916 after a proposal for an island airport reached by causeway was dropped.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and Wikipedia is not consistent with itself: it says the airport was inaugurated in 1947 but began operations in January 1948. The pages it cites for the history could not be read: the city's Atlas de Buenos Aires and aeromilitaria.com.ar no longer resolve, La Nación's 2003 article answers 404 (two addresses tried), and the Universidad de Palermo thesis is only in the blocked web archive. The operator's airport page offers only a Word download ('Descargar nota'), which the tools cannot save as text.

claims.claim: Argentina's busiest airport, 17.7 million passengers in 2025
claims.why: Held back: the old text gives no traffic figure or rank, so this replaces nothing. Aeroparque was the busiest airport in Argentina in 2025 with 17,738,000 passengers, up 19 per cent and 35 per cent of the country's total (Aviacionline, 28 January 2026, from ANAC figures; Wikipedia's infobox gives the same 17,738,000 and ranks it first; Aviacionline on 23 December 2025 also calls it the country's main airport by passengers). Worth adding if Andy agrees.
